label: copy phase: fed-back input is the digit 0
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and 98.6% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is the digit 0, i.e. the step right after the model output an original 0. A small remainder sits on d inputs right after a 0 (0 d d patterns). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or on any other token. Magnitude depends on where the 0 was in the original: activation is strongest when the 0 was original token 2-3 (recall_idx 3-4 holds 77% of mass) and drops off for earlier and later positions. It is also strongest when the token now being output is d (top activations ~4.2 are all 0 followed by d), with w, 0, i, x, l also enriched, while outputs like b, g, o, p, q, k get almost nothing. The predicate catches 97% of activations and 98.5% of mass but has low precision (~0.19), because many copy-phase 0 inputs at late positions or before non-preferred next tokens stay silent. Adding position and next-output restrictions only raises F1 to about 0.57.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 0, d, w, -, f, p; least: <DEL>, h, o, g) and the token being output (most: d, w, 0, x, i, l; least: p, t, -, j); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=4 & t=6.
